podcast.title: Advocacy and Drumming Style Impact
podcast.body: Tom Sonny Green is openly vocal about his health challenges, aiming to provide solace and support to other sufferers by letting them know they are not alone and that support groups exist. He actively collaborates with organizations like the Alport Syndrome Foundation in America, and his hearing loss offers a unique perspective on his drumming style. "Tom does work with groups like the Alport Syndrome Foundation in America."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: All-port Syndrome Diagnosis and Symptoms
podcast.body: Tom Sonny Green, the drummer for the British band Alt-J, lives with All-port syndrome, a rare genetic condition that primarily affects the kidneys, causing high levels of protein in urine and eventual end-stage renal disease. Additionally, the syndrome leads to hearing loss due to inner ear abnormalities and can affect the eyes, causing extreme sensitivity to light. "This is a rare genetic condition that starts by affecting the kidneys."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: COVID-19 Vulnerability and Illness
podcast.body: Due to All-port syndrome and the immunosuppressant drugs required for his kidney transplant, Tom Sonny Green is classified as extremely vulnerable to COVID-19, necessitating rigorous health vigilance. Despite his carefulness, he contracted a severe case of COVID in the summer of 2021, which led to a week-long hospitalization and left him debilitated for four months. "Having all-port syndrome classifies him as being extremely vulnerable to COVID, so he's had to be vigilant about staying healthy."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Lifelong Hearing Loss and Kidney Transplant
podcast.body: Tom Sonny Green experienced about 80% hearing loss by the age of six and has been a lifelong wearer of hearing aids. His kidney issues progressed to the point where he had been on dialysis since he was 19, eventually requiring a life-saving kidney transplant in 2008. He continues to rely on numerous medications to sustain his health and life. "He lost about 80% of his hearing by the time he was 6."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
